text:
tariq: Quick q — do we bump the patch for docs/packaging-only changes? I pushed a tiny changelog + packaging tweak and want to avoid churn if we can

jordan: my take: if it doesn't change runtime/consumer-visible behavior, skip bump. But tag it for traceability.

mira: yup. Bump when public API, CLI flags, config schema, or any consumer-facing surface changes. Pure README/docs/typo -> no patch bump.

sylvia: +1. Also prefer annotated tags even for "no bump" traceability: tag the commit with a note but don't publish a release artifact unless bumped. Keeps audit trail. :thumbsup:

tariq: edgecases tho — what about build/system packaging changes (dockerfile tweaks)? they can affect customers on Dedicated if they pull image by tag. If Dedicated customers pin images, we should bump patch or coordinate.

jordan: good call. Rule: bump patch if any change can affect pinned deployments or semantics. If it's purely CI infra (dev pipeline) -> no bump.

mira: security/backport case is obvious: bump patch, make hotfix branch, and ship asap.

ci-deploy-bot: deploy: canary started for v1.4.8 -> routing 5% traffic; window=10m; smoke tests running.

sylvia: tagging convention proposal: use vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH annotated tags. Avoid buildmeta in the tag name. Store release notes in repo under /releases/vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.md and link to the tag. Example:

```
# tag and push
git tag -a v1.4.8 -m "chore(release): v1.4.8 — docs + packaging"
git push origin v1.4.8
```
Add a short release note file with the PR link.

tariq: deps question — devDeps-only updates: no bump. runtime deps: bump patch if there's any behavior or transitive change. We should call out "lockfile-only" updates too — generally no bump unless they affect runtime.

jordan: also add branch naming rules for hotfixes: `hotfix/vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and backport PRs target the maint branch.

mira: rollback criteria we currently run on: error-rate > 1% OR p99 latency increase > 200ms during canary -> auto rollback. Can we codify that in the RFC?

sylvia: yes. Also add manual override thresholds and an on-call ack requirement for forced-rollbacks. Put smoke tests into the canary pipeline so infra can flip instantly.

ci-deploy-bot: status: canary healthy at T+6m. monitoring -> no regressions.

tariq: sweet. I'll update RELEASES.md with the rules:
- bump patch for consumer-visible changes, pinned-deployment-impacting changes, security/backports
- no bump for README/docs/dev-only CI changes
- annotate tags for all release-worthy commits (even if no artifact published)
- hotfix branches named `hotfix/vX.Y.Z`
- release notes under /releases/vX.Y.Z.md with PR list
- canary: 5% for 10m, rollback if errors>1% or p99+200ms

mira: add step to announce in #eng-releases and #eng-oncall when a patch ship starts and when it completes.

sylvia: checklist: changelog entry, release-notes file, tag pushed, CI canary green, announce. I'll add a template PR checklist.

tariq: cool — thanks. I'll make the PR with the RFC updates and link it here. :rocket:

ci-deploy-bot: deploy: canary completed, promoted to 100% for v1.4.8.

jordan: nice. can we add a note for Dedicated customers to include pinned-manifest updates in the hotfix PR? saves a separate update later.

mira: agreed. thanks everyone.

tariq: updating RFC now and will ping when done.

sylvia: thanks — this feels much clearer. :white_check_mark:
